name: Slagline Salvage Parka — Quilted Shell
description: A floor-length parka assembled from reclaimed industrial insulation batting, mismatched ripstop panels, and heat-tape seams. The outer shell is a patchwork of burnt orange, oil-grey, and faded safety yellow — whatever was available. Stuffed dense enough to trap body heat against -30C wind chill, though the fit is rough and the zipper skips every third tooth.
functionality: Extreme cold insulation rated for sub-zero wind chill; oversized cut fits over bulky chrome arms and spinal rigs without modification.
what_it_says: Survival over style — this person is fighting the lake wind with whatever they could pull together.
story_hooks: A hidden inner pocket contains a folded transit map with three locations marked in grease pencil — none of them transit stops.
The insulation batting is stamped with a Ferrochem facility code; someone cut this out of a condemned building's wall.
